spinophorosaurus:enwiki:8.title: Spinophorosaurus (Girdles, limbs, and misidentified tail spikes)

facts.statement: Two specimens of Spinophorosaurus were excavated in the 2000s by German and Spanish teams working under difficult conditions.
facts.quote: The first two specimens were excavated in the 2000s by German and Spanish teams under difficult conditions.

facts.statement: The first skeleton was designated the holotype specimen for the new genus and species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis in 2009.
facts.quote: The first skeleton was made the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis in 2009

facts.statement: The generic name Spinophorosaurus means "spine-bearing lizard," a name based on structures initially thought to be spiked osteoderms.
facts.quote: The generic name ("spine-bearing lizard") refers to what was initially thought to be spiked osteoderms

facts.statement: The subadult holotype specimen is estimated to be around 13 meters long, while the paratype is about 14 meters long.
facts.quote: The subadult holotype specimen is estimated to have been around 13 m in length, whereas the paratype was about 14 m long.

facts.statement: The shoulder height of these individuals is estimated at around 4 meters, and their weight at about 7 metric tons.
facts.quote: The shoulder height reached by these individuals was estimated at around 4 m, and the weight at about 7 MT.

facts.statement: The teeth were spatulate (spoon-shaped) with large spaced denticles at the crown top, representing an ancestral feature in sauropods.
facts.quote: The teeth were spatulate (spoon shaped) and had large spaced denticles at the top of the crown, an ancestral feature in sauropods.

facts.statement: The official excavation campaign, dubbed "Projekt Dino," started on March 1, 2007, traveling via Spain, Morocco, Mauritania, and Mali due to security risks in the Sahara.
facts.quote: The official campaign, dubbed "Projekt Dino", started on 1 March 2007, when two trucks with equipment left Braunschweig for Niger, taking a route via Spain, Morocco, Mauritania, and Mali (the shorter route through the Sahara was not possible due to the risk of terrorist attacks).

facts.statement: Excavation was usually interrupted between 12:00 and 15:00 when temperatures reached 43 to 45 degrees Celsius.
facts.quote: Excavation was usually interrupted between 12:00 and 15:00 when temperatures reached 43 – 45 °C.

facts.statement: On March 25, all but two members of the German team fell ill with diarrhea and circulation problems.
facts.quote: On 25 March, all but two of the German team members were ill, suffering diarrhoea and circulation problems.

facts.statement: One study suggests Spinophorosaurus may have been a high browser, while another examined possible mating postures.
facts.quote: One study suggests it may have been a high browser, and another examined possible mating postures.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus is known from the Irhazer Shale, a geological formation thought to be of Middle Jurassic age.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus is known from the Irhazer Shale, a geological formation thought to be Middle Jurassic in age.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the bones on the tail tip were spiked osteoderms or clavicles.
facts.quote: Bones originally thought to be osteoderms bearing spikes placed on the tail tip were later suggested to be clavicles.

facts.statement: The excavation of the first Spinophorosaurus skeleton was completed on April 2, and the fossils were transported to the port of Cotonou on April 3.
facts.quote: Excavation was completed on 2 April, and the fossils were packed for transport to the port of Cotonou on 3 April.

facts.statement: A large fossil block left in the field after the initial excavation was retrieved by the German team in 2008.
facts.quote: The German team retrieved the block the next season in 2008

facts.statement: German paleontologist Kristian Remes and colleagues described the species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis in 2009 using a holotype specimen split between the Elche and Braunschweig museums.
facts.quote: The first skeleton (divided between the Elche museum, where it was catalogued as GCP-CV-4229, and the Braunschweig museum, catalogued as NMB-1699-R) was made the holotype of the new genus and species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis by German palaeontologist Kristian Remes and colleagues of the German and Spanish teams in 2009.

facts.statement: The name Spinophorosaurus means "spine-bearing lizard" and originally referred to structures thought to be spiked osteoderms, though these were later suggested to be clavicles.
facts.quote: The generic name is composed of spina, Latin for "spike"; , Greek for "to bear"; and sauros, which means lizard ("spine-bearing lizard" in full): the name refers to what was initially interpreted as osteoderms bearing spikes, which were later suggested to represent clavicles instead.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a nearly complete postcranial skeleton and several skull bones but is missing the sternum, forelimb bones, and foot bones.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen consists of a braincase, a postorbital bone, a squamosal, a quadrate, a pterygoid, a surangular, and a nearly complete postcranial skeleton, which lacks the sternum, antebrachium, manus, and pes.

facts.statement: A small sauropod skeleton found near the main Spinophorosaurus specimens was reported in 2012 and is likely a juvenile of the same species.
facts.quote: In 2012, Adrián Páramo and Francisco Ortega from the PALDES team reported a small sauropod skeleton (specimen GCP-CV-BB-15) that had been discovered on the ground, a few metres from the two Spinophorosaurus specimens

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was initially estimated to be about 13 meters long, while the larger paratype was estimated at 14 meters.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was initially estimated to have been around 13 m in length when measured along the vertebral column, while the paratype was about 13 per cent larger, measuring around 14 m.

facts.statement: A later 3D photogrammetry model measured the holotype skeleton at 11.7 meters from head to tail, differing from earlier 2D estimates.
facts.quote: A later 3D photogrammetry model of the holotype skeleton measures 11.7 m from head to tail, the proportions differing from estimates based on 2D skeletal reconstructions.

facts.statement: In 2023, the holotype was listed as 11 meters long, the paratype as 13 meters, and the juvenile as 3 meters.
facts.quote: In 2023, Vidal listed the holotype as 11 m long, the paratype as 13 m, and the juvenile as 3 m.

facts.statement: The shoulder height of Spinophorosaurus is estimated at around 4 meters and its weight at about 7 metric tons.
facts.quote: The shoulder height reached by these individuals was estimated at around 4 m, and the weight at about 7 MT.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a subadult indicated by unfused sutures, while the paratype has fully fused sutures indicating adulthood.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen's endocranial and neurocentral sutures in the skull and vertebrae respectively are unfused, indicating it was a subadult, whereas the paratype specimen has fully fused neurocentral sutures.

facts.statement: The basal tubera were enlarged and directed to the sides, a feature unique among known sauropods.
facts.quote: The basal tubera (a pair of extensions on the underside of the skull base that served as muscle attachments) were enlarged and were directed to the sides, unique among known sauropods.

facts.statement: The trunk consisted of 12 dorsal and four sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: The trunk had 12 dorsal and four sacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae had large excavations on their sides called pleurocoels that deepened towards the front.
facts.quote: The cervical centra had large excavations on their sides that deepened towards the front; such pleurocoels were also developed in Jobaria and Patagosaurus.

facts.statement: A U-shaped depression between the centrum and the neural arch in side view is a unique feature of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: In side view, a U-shaped depression was present between the centrum and the neural arch, which is an autapomorphy (unique feature) of Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: The chevrons in the front part of the tail were blade-like, representing the basal condition.
facts.quote: In the front part of the tail, the chevrons (paired bones below the vertebral centra) were blade-like, which is the basal condition.

facts.statement: The rod-like chevrons in the rear tail were closely attached to the centra and articulated at the mid-length of the vertebral centra, bracing the joint and restricting tail bending.
facts.quote: These rod-like chevrons would have been closely attached to the bottom edges of the centra. They articulated with the preceding and succeeding chevrons at the mid length of the vertebral centra, thus bracing the vertebral joint, restricting bending of the tail.

facts.statement: The open postparietal notch on the skull rear margin is a feature shared with dicraeosaurids and Abrosaurus.
facts.quote: The rear margin of the skull had an open postparietal notch, a feature otherwise only known in dicraeosaurids and Abrosaurus.

facts.statement: The broad upper temporal fenestrae are typical of Shunosaurus and more derived sauropods.
facts.quote: The upper temporal fenestrae, a pair of major openings on the skull roof, were four times broader than long; such broadened fenestrae were typical for Shunosaurus and more derived (or "advanced") sauropods.

facts.statement: The neuroanatomy is intermediate between basal sauropodomorphs and more derived neosauropods.
facts.quote: Its neuroanatomy was in some ways intermediate between that of basal (or "primitive") sauropodomorphs and the more derived neosauropods.

facts.statement: The shoulder blade of Spinophorosaurus was strongly curved with a fan-shaped lower end, a feature unique among sauropods.
facts.quote: The scapula was unique amongst sauropods, being strongly curved with an expanded, fan-shaped lower end.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone of Spinophorosaurus had a distinct kidney shape that is considered a unique trait of the species.
facts.quote: The coracoid, which articulated to the lower end of the scapula, showed a distinct kidney-shape, considered an autapomorphy.

facts.statement: A large opening near the fourth trochanter on the thigh bone is absent in other sauropods and is a unique trait of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Close to the fourth trochanter was a large opening that is absent in other sauropods, and thus an autapomorphy.

facts.statement: Bones originally thought to be osteoderms were found with the main skeleton of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Elements originally interpreted as a left and right osteoderm (bone formed in the skin) were found with the holotype skeleton.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that structures originally interpreted as tail spikes or osteoderms in Spinophorosaurus may actually be clavicles rather than armor.
facts.quote: In 2013, palaeontologists Emanuel Tschopp and Octávio Mateus reexamined the supposed tail spikes and found they did not have the typical rugose surface of osteoderms seen in other armoured dinosaurs, or the club-like expansion seen in Shunosaurus.

facts.statement: Early studies classified Spinophorosaurus as one of the most primitive sauropods, closely related to Vulcanodon, Cetiosaurus, and Tazoudasaurus.
facts.quote: The initial phylogenetic analysis presented by Remes and colleagues suggested Spinophorosaurus fell among the most basal sauropods known, being only slightly more derived than Vulcanodon, Cetiosaurus, and Tazoudasaurus.

facts.statement: A 2022 study proposes that Spinophorosaurus is the most primitive member of the Mamenchisauridae group.
facts.quote: A 2022 study by palaeontologist Xin-Xin Ren and colleagues found Spinophorosaurus to be the basalmost mamenchisaurid, sharing eight derived features with this group.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus likely lived across Asia and Africa during the late Early to Middle Jurassic periods.
facts.quote: they stated it must have been widespread across Asia and Africa during the late Early to Middle Jurassic, before Laurasia and Gondwana disconnected during the late Middle to Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus shares anatomical features with Middle Jurassic East Asian sauropods but differs significantly from those found in South America and India.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus shares features with Middle Jurassic East Asian sauropods (especially in the neck and tail vertebrae, scapula and humerus) but is very dissimilar from Lower and Middle Jurassic South American and Indian taxa

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that geographic barriers separated the Middle Jurassic sauropod faunas of Laurasia and South Gondwana.
facts.quote: They suggested this could be explained by the Middle Jurassic sauropod faunas of Laurasia and South Gondwana having been separated by geographic barriers.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus possesses ancestral traits in East Asian sauropods that were previously thought to be derived features.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus shows that features once thought to be derived among East Asian sauropods are rather plesiomorphic (ancestral traits) among eusauropods

facts.statement: During the Early and Middle Jurassic, the region where Spinophorosaurus lived was close to the equator with a summer-wet climate and high plant diversity.
facts.quote: It was close to the equator and had a summer-wet climate in the Early and Middle Jurassic, with high plant productivity and diversity.

facts.statement: In 2020, Vidal and colleagues suggested that the wedged sacral vertebrae and upward-deflected vertebral column of Spinophorosaurus were ancestral features of eusauropods.
facts.quote: Vidal and colleagues suggested in 2020 that the wedged sarcral vertebrae and upward deflecected vertebral column of Spinophorosaurus was an ancestral feature of eusauropods

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus retained a non-reduced vestibular apparatus in its inner ear, which is unusual for heavy plant-eating quadrupeds.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus and some other sauropodomorphs did not have reduced vestibular apparatuses, a sensory system for balance and orientation in the inner ear

facts.statement: An adult Spinophorosaurus specimen was found to contain radial fibrolamellar bone in the outermost layer of its humerus, a feature previously unreported in sauropods.
facts.quote: At a 2018 conference, Benjamin Jentgen-Ceschino and colleagues reported radial fibrolamellar bone (RFB), a type of bone tissue characterised by radially oriented channels, in the outermost part of the cortex (the outermost bone layer) of the humerus belonging to an adult Spinophorosaurus specimen

facts.statement: The presence of radial fibrolamellar bone in the outer cortex of an adult Spinophorosaurus suggests the animal survived for some time after an injury caused accelerated bone growth.
facts.quote: The RFB of the Spinophorosaurus was buried in the outer cortex, followed by a normal fibrolamellar complex, which indicates the animal survived for some time after its accelerated growth, which probably suggests pathological bone growth due to injury.

facts.statement: A 2015 study using a 3D model found that the frontmost 20 tail vertebrae of Spinophorosaurus could deflect up to 20 degrees and sideways flex by 8 to 10 degrees.
facts.quote: Manipulation of the 3D model by Vidal and colleagues in 2015 showed that each of the frontmost 20 tail vertebrae could deflect up to 20º, and 8–10º in sideways flexion, before limited by the bone morphology.

facts.statement: Researchers Joger and colleagues argued in 2009 that the tail spikes of Spinophorosaurus formed a thagomiser used for defense against predators.
facts.quote: Joger and colleagues argued in 2009 that the supposed spikes formed a thagomiser at the end of the tail that would have been used for defence against predators.

facts.statement: According to Vidal, "backwards mating" was the only possible method for sauropods to mate without a male intromittent organ.
facts.quote: "Backwards mating" is the only way sauropods could have mated without the need of a male intromittent organ.

facts.statement: In 2020, Vidal and colleagues used 3D models of the holotype and juvenile skeletons to estimate the neck flexibility of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Vidal and colleagues, in 2020, used 3D models of both the holotype and the juvenile skeleton to estimate the range of motion (flexibility) of the neck.

facts.statement: As Spinophorosaurus grew, its neck range of motion increased, the gaps between vertebrae widened, and the neck became more inclined in a neutral posture.
facts.quote: As Spinophorosaurus grew, the range of motion of the neck would increase (making steeper neck postures possible); the gap between vertebrae become larger; and the neck become more inclined in neutral posture.

facts.statement: Anatomical features such as a narrow snout, broad teeth, and a long humerus suggest Spinophorosaurus was adapted for high browsing.
facts.quote: High browsing is also suggested by anatomical features, including the narrow snout, broad teeth, and proportionally long humerus compared to the scapula.

facts.statement: Although Spinophorosaurus had flexible vertebral articulations, its elongated cervical ribs might have prevented it from bending its neck sideways against its body while sleeping like giraffes.
facts.quote: While sleeping, giraffes bend their necks sideways against the body. Although the vertebral articulations would have been flexible enough for such bending in Spinophorosaurus, it might have been prohibited by the elongated cervical ribs.

facts.statement: Four theropod teeth were found near the holotype skeleton, three resembling Megalosauridae or Allosauridae and one possibly belonging to an early Spinosaurid.
facts.quote: Four theropod teeth were found closely associated with the Spinophorosaurus holotype (by a vertebra, pubis, and in the acetabulum)

facts.statement: Dinosaur tracks found near the site include a six-footprint trackway from a mid-sized sauropod and 120 two-toed theropod footprints.
facts.quote: Dinosaur tracks were found some hundred metres away from the Spinophorosaurus site, including a trackway of six footprints from a mid-sized sauropod as well as 120 well-preserved didactyl (two-toed) theropod footprints.

facts.statement: Its stratigraphic and phylogenetic position suggests Spinophorosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bajocian to Bathonian stages.
facts.quote: The stratigraphical and phylogenetic position of Spinophorosaurus (compared with other basal sauropods from around the world) indicates it could be Middle Jurassic (Bajocian–Bathonian) in age.

facts.statement: The animal lived in a fluvio-lacustrine environment where the Iullemmeden Basin was connected to the Proto-Atlantic coast of Gondwana.
facts.quote: Sediments of the Irhazer Group were deposited under conditions that were fluvio-lacustrine (associated with rivers and lakes), during a time when the Iullemmeden Basin was part of a great river-valley system, which was connected with the Proto-Atlantic coast of Gondwana through adjacent basins.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis is one of the most complete basal sauropod specimens known, and it is the first of its type discovered in Africa.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de este género, Spinophorosaurus nigerensis, es uno de los ejemplares de saurópodo basales más completos recuperados hasta ahora, junto a los descubrimientos en China y América del Sur, además de ser el primero de su tipo hallado en el continente africano.

facts.statement: It lived approximately 167 million years ago during the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 167 millones de años durante el Bathoniense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was about 13 meters long along the spine, while the paratype was about 13 percent larger at 14 meters.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo tenía alrededor de 13 metros de largo cuando se mide a lo largo de la columna vertebral, mientras que el paratipo era aproximadamente un 13 por ciento más grande, midiendo alrededor de 14 metros.

facts.statement: A 3D photogrammetry model of the holotype measures 11.7 meters from head to tail, differing from 2D skeletal reconstruction estimates.
facts.quote: Un modelo de fotogrametría 3D del esqueleto holotipo mide 11,7 metros de la cabeza a la cola, las proporciones difieren de las estimaciones basadas en reconstrucciones esqueléticas 2D.

facts.statement: The shoulder height of these individuals is estimated at around 4 meters and the weight at around 7 tons.
facts.quote: La altura de los hombros alcanzada por estos individuos se estimó en alrededor de 4 metros, y el peso en alrededor de 7 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2020, researchers revised the posture of Spinophorosaurus to be more vertical with high shoulders and an elevated neck, based on digital skeletal assembly.
facts.quote: En 2020, Vidal y sus colegas revisaron la postura de Spinophorosaurus, basándose en el montaje del esqueleto digital. Mientras que la reconstrucción esquelética original de 2009 mostraba al dinosaurio con una postura horizontal, la reconstrucción digital mostró una postura más vertical, con hombros altos y un cuello elevado.

facts.statement: Consequently, the snout of Spinophorosaurus would have been held about 5 meters above the ground, more than double the height of the shoulders and acetabulum at 2.15 meters.
facts.quote: En consecuencia, el hocico del Spinophorosaurus se habría sostenido a unos 5 metros sobre el suelo, más del doble de la altura de los hombros y el acetábulo donde la pata trasera se unía a la pelvis, que estaban a una altura de 2,15 metros.

facts.statement: The genus Spinophorosaurus was named by Remes and colleagues in 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Remes et al., 2009

facts.statement: The species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis was named by Remes and colleagues in 2009.
facts.quote: species_authority: Remes et al., 2009

facts.statement: Many characteristics linking it to the African Tazoudasaurus present Spinophorosaurus as a typical basal sauropod of southern Gondwana.
facts.quote: Muchas de las características que lo relacionan con el también africano Tazoudasaurus presentan a Spinophorosaurus como un saurópodo basal típico del sur de Gondwana.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the "advanced" features linking Spinophorosaurus to Eurasian eusauropods like Shunosaurus or Mamenchisauridae indicate simultaneous development or simple inheritance.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, este género también presenta características "avanzadas" que lo relacionan con algunos saurópodos euroasiáticos eusaurópodos, como Shunosaurus o Mamenchisauridae.

facts.statement: In the holotype specimen, the frontal bones of the skull roof were fused in the midline, unlike other skull sutures.
facts.quote: En el ejemplar holotipo los huesos frontales del techo del cráneo estaban fusionados en la línea media, a diferencia de las otras suturas del cráneo.

facts.statement: A small pineal foramen was located about 10 millimeters in front of the suture between the frontal and parietal bones.
facts.quote: Entre los frontales había un pequeño agujero pineal , a unos 10 milímetros por delante de la sutura entre el frontal y los huesos parietales.

facts.statement: The posterior margin of the skull had an open postparietal notch, a feature otherwise known only in dicraeosaurids and Abrosaurus.
facts.quote: El margen posterior del cráneo tenía una muesca postparietal abierta, una característica que de otro modo solo se conoce en dicreosáuridos y Abrosaurus.

facts.statement: The upper temporal windows, a pair of main openings in the skull roof, were four times wider than they were long.
facts.quote: Las ventanas temporales superiores, un par de aberturas principales en el techo del cráneo, eran cuatro veces más anchas que largas.

facts.statement: The skull box of Spinophorosaurus was wide and short from front to back, moderately deep, and of relatively large size in general.
facts.quote: La caja craneana del Spinophorosaurus era ancha y corta de adelante hacia atrás, moderadamente profunda y de tamaño relativamente grande en general.

facts.statement: The inner ear labyrinth was characterized by having long and thin semicircular canals, similar to those of Massospondylus and Giraffatitan.
facts.quote: El laberinto del oído interno se caracterizaba por tener canales semicirculares largos y delgados , similares a los de Massospondylus y Giraffatitan.

facts.statement: The neck was composed of 13 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: El cuello estaba compuesto por 13 vértebras cervicales .

facts.statement: The vertebral column is known almost completely, and the holotype is one of the few sauropod specimens that include a complete neck.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral se conoce casi por completo, y el holotipo es uno de los pocos especímenes de saurópodo que incluyen un cuello completo.

facts.statement: The cervical centers had large excavations on their sides that deepened towards the front.
facts.quote: Los centros cervicales tenían grandes excavaciones en sus costados que se profundizaban hacia el frente.

facts.statement: In lateral view, a U-shaped depression was present between the centrum and the neural arch, which is an autapomorphy of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: En vista lateral, una depresión en forma de U estaba presente entre el centro y el arco neural, que es una autapomorfia de Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae were unusual for having a honeycomb internal structure containing multiple small air-filled chambers.
facts.quote: Las vértebras dorsales eran inusuales por tener una estructura interna camelada, que contenía múltiples cámaras pequeñas llenas de aire.

facts.statement: The ribs from the second to fifth dorsal vertebrae were flattened and directed backward, while those from the sixth to eleventh dorsal vertebrae had a more circular cross-section and a more vertical orientation.
facts.quote: Las costillas de la segunda a la quinta vértebra dorsal estaban aplanadas y dirigidas hacia atrás, mientras que las de la sexta a la undécima dorsal tenían una sección transversal más circular y una orientación más vertical.

facts.statement: At the rear of the tail, the chevrons were like rods, and the left and right counterparts were separated from each other.
facts.quote: En la parte trasera de la cola, los galones eran como varillas, y las contrapartes izquierda y derecha estaban separadas entre sí.

facts.statement: These rod-shaped chevrons would have been closely attached to the lower edges of the centrum.
facts.quote: Estos galones en forma de varilla habrían estado estrechamente unidos a los bordes inferiores del centro.

facts.statement: They articulated with the anterior and posterior chevrons at the midpoint of the vertebral centrum lengths, thereby reinforcing the vertebral articulation and restricting tail flexibility.
facts.quote: Se articulaban con los galones anteriores y posteriores en la mitad de la longitud de los centros vertebrales, reforzando así la articulación vertebral y restringiendo la flexión de la cola.

facts.statement: Its scapula was unique among sauropods, being strongly curved with a lower end expanded like a fan.
facts.quote: La escápula era única entre los saurópodos, estaba fuertemente curvada con un extremo inferior expandido en forma de abanico.

facts.statement: The coracoid, articulating at the bottom of the scapula, had a distinctive kidney shape considered an autapomorphy.
facts.quote: El coracoides, que se articulaba en el extremo inferior de la escápula, mostraba una forma distintiva de riñón, considerada una autapomorfía.

facts.statement: The fourth trochanter, projecting from the rear surface to anchor muscles pulling the hind leg backward, was especially large in Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: El cuarto trocánter , que se proyectaba desde la superficie posterior y anclaba los músculos que tiraban de la pata trasera hacia atrás, era especialmente grande en Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: Near the fourth trochanter was a large opening absent in other sauropods, making it an autapomorphy.
facts.quote: Cerca del cuarto trocánter había una gran abertura que está ausente en otros saurópodos y, por lo tanto, una autapomorfía.

facts.statement: A cladogram by Nair and Salisbury (2012) supports a basal position for Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Cladograma basado en Nair y Salisbury, 2012, que respalda una posición basal de Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: A cladogram by Xing and colleagues (2015) supports a more derived position within Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Cladograma basado en Xing y colegas, 2015, que respalda una posición más derivada dentro de Eusauropoda.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Gravisauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gravisauria

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: It lived from the Bajocian to the Bathonian stages, between 170.9 and 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bathonian (170.9 to 165.3 million years ago)

rejected.quote: A juvenile sauropod from the same area was later assigned to the genus.
